Listing schedule

Area data

English Indices of Deprivation 2025 (MHCLG) for all neighbourhoods (2021 LSOAs) in England, drawn for the districts you choose. Decile 1 is the most deprived tenth of England; decile 10 the least. Where most of a district sits in the same few deciles, the second shading mode ranks the neighbourhoods on the map against each other. Crystal Roof scores are theirs, quoted for the example postcodes with the date they were read.

The map

Boundaries are the ONS generalised set, so edges are approximate, and each pin is placed where the portal's own map puts the listing, or at the postcode centre when it gives no position. Drag a pin to correct it. Colours follow the government's Local Deprivation Explorer; this is not an official page.

Listing records

Records come from the public listing pages on the date shown. Reading a link fills in what that page shows. Both portals show only their most recent change, so an earlier listing date or price may be missing. Earlier adverts and sold prices come from Zoopla's page for the address, which is matched by house number or as the nearest address to the pin, so confirm the address before relying on them.

What this is not

A decile or an area rating describes an area, not a house, and none of this is a valuation, a survey or legal advice. The points to check are prompts to raise with the agent, your conveyancer and your surveyor.
